pr_metadata.title: [REVIEW] Enable merge/set_index for cudf-based dataframes with cupy `values`
pr_metadata.description:
This PR is a continuation of #5205, with the goal of allowing `rearrange_by_divisions`, `set_index`, `merge`, etc... to be used with `cudf`-based dataframes.  Due to recent progressin cudf, this requires two general changes:

1. cudf dataframe/series `.values` will soon return cupy (rather than numpy) arrays.  Since the pandas' `groupsort_indexer` function requires numpy, we need to check for a `values_host` attribute right before this function is called.  A cudf drop-in for `groupsort_indexer` is in progress, but the use of `values_host` is needed until then.

2. Since `hash_pandas_object` does not work for cudf dataframes,  we need to use `cudf.hash_columns` (when the attribute is available) within `partitioning_index`.  Note that this is required for `merge` to work with cudf-based dataframes.

cc @brandon-b-miller - These changes *should* allow dask_cudf tests to pass for [cudf#2655](https://github.com/rapidsai/cudf/pull/2655)

- [ ] Tests added / passed
- [ ] Passes `black dask` / `flake8 dask`

I think that this function may not be necessary, the `hash_df_dispatch` object above should do this.  You might remove this function and rename the dispatch object above.

We had to do tricky dispatch stuff with `concat` (where I expect you're copying things from) because `concat` takes in a list, and so it's harder to dispatch on types.
